QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of business
Options: A) Dealing in goods and services
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Business involves regular dealings in goods and services, not one-time transactions. Regularity of transactions is an essential characteristic of business.

QuestionText: The primary objective of a business is to:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: The primary objective of any business is to earn profit. Without profit, a business cannot survive in the long run.

QuestionText: Ravi operates a grocery store from his home and manages all activities himself. He enjoys all profits but also bears all losses. Which form of business organization is this
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A sole proprietorship is owned and managed by a single person who bears all risks and enjoys all profits.

QuestionText: In a partnership firm, the relationship between partners is based on:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Partnership is formed through mutual agreement between two or more persons who agree to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all.

QuestionText: The maximum number of partners allowed in a banking business partnership is:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: As per the Companies Act, the maximum number of partners in a banking business is 10, while for other businesses it is 50.

QuestionText: Which document contains the rules and regulations for internal management of a company
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Articles of Association contains rules and regulations for internal management and administration of the company.

QuestionText: A Joint Hindu Family Business is governed by:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Joint Hindu Family Business is governed by Hindu Law and membership is acquired by birth into the family.

QuestionText: Which of the following is a feature of cooperative societies
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Cooperative societies are formed with a service motive to provide mutual help to members, not profit maximization.

QuestionText: The liability of members in a Joint Stock Company is:
Options: B) Limited to the extent of capital contribution
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In a Joint Stock Company, the liability of members is limited to the extent of their capital contribution or the unpaid amount on shares held by them.

QuestionText: Disinvestment refers to:
Options: B) Sale of government equity in public enterprises
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Disinvestment means the sale of government equity or stake in public sector enterprises to private investors.

QuestionText: A company that operates in more than one country is known as:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A Multinational Corporation (MNC) is a company that has business operations in multiple countries beyond its home country.

QuestionText: The Memorandum of Association is also known as:
Options: A) Birth certificate of a company
C) Death certificate of a company
D) Rule book of a company
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: The Memorandum of Association is called the Charter of a company as it defines the scope and powers of the company.

QuestionText: Which type of partner contributes capital and shares profits but does not participate in management
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A sleeping or dormant partner contributes capital and shares profits but does not take part in the day-to-day management of the firm.

QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT a type of cooperative society
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Monopoly cooperative is not a recognized type. Common types include consumer, producer, marketing, credit, and housing cooperatives.

QuestionText: A public company must have a minimum paid-up capital of:
Options: D) No minimum requirement after Companies Amendment Act 2015
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: After the Companies Amendment Act 2015, there is no minimum paid-up capital requirement for public or private companies.

QuestionText: In a Joint Hindu Family Business, the head of the family who manages the business is called:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In a Joint Hindu Family Business, the eldest member who manages the business is called the Karta.

QuestionText: Which of the following businesses has the least legal formalities for formation
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Sole proprietorship has minimum legal formalities as no registration is compulsory and it can be started with minimal procedures.

QuestionText: Prospectus is issued by a company to:
Options: C) General public for subscription of shares
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A prospectus is an invitation to the public to subscribe for shares or debentures of the company.

QuestionText: The voting principle in a cooperative society is:
Options: C) Votes based on capital contribution
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In cooperative societies, the principle of one member one vote is followed, irrespective of the number of shares held.

QuestionText: Government company is one in which the government holds more than:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A Government company is one in which at least 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government or State Government or both.

QuestionText: Anita, Beena, and Chitra started a boutique business together. They agreed to share profits in the ratio 3:2:1. After six months, the business incurred a loss of Rs. 60,000. How much loss will Chitra bear
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Chitra's share = 1/(3+2+1) x 60,000 = 1/6 x 60,000 = Rs. 10,000. Partners share losses in their profit-sharing ratio.

QuestionText: ABC Ltd. was incorporated on March 1, 2023. It received certificate of commencement of business on April 15, 2023. The company can start its business operations from:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A public company can commence business only after obtaining the certificate of commencement of business, which is April 15, 2023 in this case.

QuestionText: Mr. Kumar introduced his friend to a partnership firm as a partner, although the friend had no actual involvement. Later, a creditor extended credit based on this representation. The friend is a:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A partner by estoppel is someone who represents himself or allows himself to be represented as a partner, though he is not actually a partner.

QuestionText: XYZ Cooperative Society has 500 members. For a resolution to be passed, at least 60% members must vote in favor. The minimum number of votes required to pass a resolution is:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: 60% of 500 = 300 votes. Since cooperative societies follow one member one vote principle, 300 members must vote in favor.

QuestionText: A multinational company headquartered in USA has subsidiaries in India, UK, and Japan. The company earned Rs. 50 crores in India but reported losses in UK and Japan. For Indian taxation purposes:
Options: A) The company pays tax only on Indian profits
B) The company pays tax on global profits
D) Tax is paid only in USA
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In India, an MNC pays tax only on the income earned within India. Global profits are not taxed in India.

QuestionText: Ramesh, a Karta of a Joint Hindu Family Business, took a loan of Rs. 10 lakhs for business expansion. The business failed and could not repay the loan. The liability of other coparceners is:
Options: B) Limited to their share in joint family property
D) Equal to the Karta's liability
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In a HUF business, coparceners have limited liability to the extent of their share in the joint family property, while Karta has unlimited liability.

QuestionText: Which clause of the Memorandum of Association cannot be altered under any circumstances
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: The subscription clause (also called association clause) stating the intention to form a company cannot be altered once the company is formed.

QuestionText: Five farmers formed a cooperative society to sell their produce collectively. This type of cooperative is called:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Marketing cooperatives are formed by producers to sell their products collectively and get better prices.

QuestionText: The minimum number of persons required to form a public company is:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A minimum of 7 persons are required to form a public company as per the Companies Act, 2013.

QuestionText: Business risk refers to:
Options: A) Possibility of inadequate profits or losses
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Business risk refers to the possibility of inadequate profits or even losses due to uncertainties such as change in consumer preferences, competition, etc.

QuestionText: Which of the following is an economic objective of business
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Earning profit is an economic objective. Other options are social objectives of business.

QuestionText: A private limited company can have a maximum of how many members
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: As per Companies Act 2013, a private limited company can have a maximum of 200 members, excluding past and present employees who are members.

QuestionText: Registration of a partnership firm is:
Options: D) Required only for large firms
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Registration of partnership firm is not compulsory but is advisable as an unregistered firm faces certain legal disabilities.

QuestionText: Star Electronics Ltd. is planning to issue shares to the public for the first time. Before doing so, it must file which document with the Registrar of Companies
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Before issuing shares to public, a company must file a prospectus with the Registrar of Companies containing all material information about the company.

QuestionText: In case of dissolution of a partnership firm, the private debts of partners are paid:
Options: A) Before firm's debts from firm's assets
B) After firm's debts from partner's private assets
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Firm's debts are paid first from firm's assets. Private debts are paid from partners' private assets after settling firm's debts.

QuestionText: Sunrise Cooperative Credit Society charges 12% interest on loans while commercial banks charge 14%. This demonstrates which principle of cooperative societies
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Providing loans at lower interest rates demonstrates the principle of mutual help and welfare in cooperative societies.

QuestionText: Global Tech Inc., an MNC, decides to set up a wholly-owned subsidiary in India. This is an example of:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Setting up a wholly-owned subsidiary involves direct investment of capital and is classified as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI).

QuestionText: The government decided to sell 25% of its stake in a public sector enterprise to private investors. This process is called:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Disinvestment refers to the sale of government's equity in public enterprises to private investors.

QuestionText: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a Joint Stock Company
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Joint Stock Companies have limited liability of shareholders, not unlimited liability. This is one of its key features.

QuestionText: A statutory corporation is created by:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A statutory corporation is created by a Special Act of Parliament or State Legislature. Examples include LIC, RBI.

QuestionText: In a partnership at will, any partner can dissolve the firm by giving:
Options: C) Notice of his intention to all other partners
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: In a partnership at will, any partner can dissolve the firm by giving notice of his intention to all other partners.

QuestionText: The doctrine of ultra vires is related to:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Ultra vires means beyond powers. Any act done beyond the objects stated in the Memorandum of Association is void and cannot be ratified.

QuestionText: Mohan provides only his name and reputation to a partnership firm without any capital contribution. He is known as:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A nominal partner only lends his name to the firm without contributing capital or taking part in management.

QuestionText: The concept of separate legal entity means:
Options: A) Business and owner are the same
B) Business and owner are distinct in the eyes of law
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Separate legal entity means the company is distinct from its members and can own property, sue and be sued in its own name.

QuestionText: A company incorporated in India but controlled by a foreign company is called:
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: A subsidiary company is one where more than 50% of the equity share capital is held by another company (holding company).

QuestionText: Which of the following public sector enterprises operates under departmental undertaking model
Options: D) Oil and Natural Gas Corporation
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Indian Railways is a departmental undertaking that functions as a department of the government and is financed and controlled directly by the government.

QuestionText: Prakash and Suresh are partners sharing profits equally. Prakash brought Rs. 5,00,000 as capital while Suresh brought Rs. 3,00,000. The partnership deed is silent on interest on capital. What interest will Prakash receive
Options: D) As decided by partners later
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: If the partnership deed is silent on interest on capital, no interest is payable to partners as per the Partnership Act, 1932.

QuestionText: Century Textiles Ltd. wants to change its registered office from Mumbai to Delhi. This requires alteration of which clause of the Memorandum
Topic: Commerce - Nature and Forms of Business
Explanation: Change of registered office from one state to another requires alteration of the Registered Office clause with approval of Central Government.
